headline: High-risk default filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter can modify the user machine while the paired repo is non-runnable and offers no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs directly. B can read clipboard/files and execute shell, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel beyond manual copy-paste. That makes prompt injection possible only through unusual operator bridging, with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies B-generated text into A-related prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced between the agents, A can become a prompt source.
mitigations: Keep A as a static reference list only.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Use separate terminals and separate working directories.
Require human review before pasting any agent output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any shared text channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while B can read the entire local filesystem and has broad egress plus access to model-provider APIs. If B is pointed at files that A helped select or summarize, sensitive local data can leave the machine. The pair’s risk is driven by B, but the interaction is plausible in default desktop use.
conditions: IF B is given access to sensitive local files, those contents can be transmitted off-machine.
IF the operator uses A to curate filenames or paths for B, B may ingest unintended sensitive material.
mitigations: Restrict B to a dedicated non-sensitive directory.
Turn off or tightly scope B network access.
Do not pass secrets through clipboard or stdin/stdout.
Use a separate OS account for B.
requires-engineering: sandbox B with filesystem allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write capabilities, but B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell with shared state via filesystem. Because B’s defaults include unrestricted local mutation and the pair has no locking or coordination primitive, concurrent use can corrupt shared work or git history. Uncertainty is low because B’s write surfaces are explicit and A provides no isolation.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory, B can overwrite files or git state created during A-guided work.
IF multiple B instances are launched, filesystem-mediated shared state can race without locks.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace.
Pause B before any git commit or file write.
Use one B instance at a time.
Review diffs before accepting changes.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace management.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can provide curated recommendations or summaries, and B can act on them with shell and filesystem authority. There is no documented verification loop between them, so B may treat A’s output as authoritative and propagate mistakes into files or commands. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than immediate irreversible harm, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated recommendations without independent verification, errors can cascade into executed commands or edited files.
IF A is used to summarize external guidance for B, B may operationalize incorrect summaries.
mitigations: Require B to verify A’s claims against source material.
Keep A outputs advisory, not authoritative.
Add a human approval step before execution.
Log provenance for any A-to-B handoff.
requires-engineering: implement citation checks before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source reference list with no touched data classes, so it is not the compliance driver. B, however, can access anything on the local machine and send context to configured model providers, creating a residency and retention mismatch risk for local sensitive data. Because the compliance exposure is primarily from B’s default behavior, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF local files contain regulated data, B may process them outside the original residency boundary.
IF configured model providers retain prompts, local data may be logged or retained externally.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B’s workspace.
Use provider settings with minimal retention.
Route only redacted excerpts to B.
Document the data flow before deployment.
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing and retention controls.
